### The seven triples form the Fano plane

The triples

\[
\{i,i+1,i+3\}
\]

have the following standard Fano-plane properties:

- Each point lies in exactly \(3\) triples.
- Each pair of points lies in exactly one triple.
- Any two triples meet in exactly one point.

For example, each point \(i\) appears in \(L_i,L_{i-1},L_{i-3}\). Also, the differences between two elements of \(\{i,i+1,i+3\}\) are \(1,2,3\) modulo \(7\), each occurring once, so every pair of points occurs in exactly one \(L_i\). Since each point lies on only three lines, two lines cannot be disjoint: if they were disjoint, a point on one line would have to lie on three different lines through points of the other line, leaving only two available besides its own line.

We will use these facts constantly.
